name: gutfeel-mcp

tools.name: likely
tools.description:
Judge whether a claim is true of a text. Answers yes or no with the model's
        probability that the claim is true -- or unsure, when ask_human is set.

subject.description: The text to judge: an email, a comment, a diff.
subject.title: Subject

question.description: A short claim about the text, e.g. "asks for a refund". Not an open question.
question.title: Question

ask_human.description: Allow the outcome `unsure` when the model cannot tell. Off by default.
ask_human.title: Ask Human

stakes.description: How sure the model must be before an answer counts. Needs ask_human.
stakes.title: Stakes

lean.description: Which way to err when unsure is not allowed.
lean.title: Lean

tools.name: classify
tools.description:
Pick the option that fits a text best: a team, a topic, a language, an intent. Answers
        with the chosen label, every option's probability and a confidence.

subject.description: The text to judge: an email, a comment, a diff.
subject.title: Subject

options.description: The categories: {label: description}, or a list of labels. Include a catch-all such as "other", or every text is forced into one of them.
options.title: Options

question.description: What to decide, if the options do not say it.
question.title: Question

ask_human.description: Allow the outcome `unsure` when the model cannot tell. Off by default.
ask_human.title: Ask Human

stakes.description: How sure the model must be before an answer counts. Needs ask_human.
stakes.title: Stakes

tools.name: rate
tools.description:
Rate a text on an ordered scale such as urgency or severity. Answers with a score,
        which can fall between levels, the nearest level and a confidence.

subject.description: The text to judge: an email, a comment, a diff.
subject.title: Subject

levels.description: Between 2 and 10 level descriptions, in order; the first is level 0.
levels.title: Levels

question.description: What to rate, if the levels do not say it.
question.title: Question

ask_human.description: Allow the outcome `unsure` when the model cannot tell. Off by default.
ask_human.title: Ask Human

stakes.description: How sure the model must be before an answer counts. Needs ask_human.
stakes.title: Stakes

tools.name: each
tools.description:
Ask the same question about many texts at once: likely with just a question, classify
        with options, rate with levels. Far faster than one call per text.

subjects.description: The texts to judge, all with the same question.
subjects.title: Subjects

question.description: A claim, as for likely. Alone, it asks likely; with options or levels, it says what to decide.
question.title: Question

ask_human.description: Allow the outcome `unsure` when the model cannot tell. Off by default.
ask_human.title: Ask Human

stakes.description: How sure the model must be before an answer counts. Needs ask_human.
stakes.title: Stakes

instructions:
gut answers judgment calls about text with a small, fast, cheap model, and says when it does not know.

Use it for questions whose answer is a judgment rather than a fact you can compute: is this comment spam, which team owns this ticket, how urgent is this email. It is at its best on many texts at once: use `each` to triage a whole inbox or a page of search results in one call, where reading every item yourself would be slow and expensive.

Every answer carries an outcome and a probability (or a confidence). `unsure` only happens when you pass ask_human=true, and means the model could not tell: read the text yourself or ask the user. Confidence is how peaked the model's answer is, not the probability that it is right.

Questions work best as short, concrete claims about the text ("asks for a refund", "is written in German"), not as open questions or judgments of quality.
